body:
`scripts/lib/phase7-envelope.sh:84` does:

    text="$(printf '%s' "$last" | jq -r '.result // ""' | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-160)"

The launchd plist sets PATH, HOME and USER but NOT LANG, so the tick runs in the C locale,
where `cut -c` counts BYTES rather than characters. Non-ASCII model output longer than 160
bytes is therefore sliced mid-UTF-8-sequence.

Severity is deliberately `chore`, not `correctness`: `$text` is only used for ASCII substring
matching (`*"Not logged in"*` and friends, which a tail-end split does not affect) and for
interpolation into an operator-facing error string. The realistic worst case is mojibake in a
page that only fires when phase-7 has already failed.

Recorded because it is the same defect class as the Discord one fixed on 2026-08-08, where it
DID matter: `discord_start_thread` and the triage title/question caps used the identical
`tr -d … | cut -c1-N` spelling and would have sent Discord undecodable bytes for any non-ASCII
report title over the cap. That was replaced with a `discord_clip` python3 helper, because
python3 auto-enables UTF-8 mode in the C locale (PEP 540, `sys.flags.utf8_mode == 1`).

Measured 2026-08-08 on a 150-character CJK string: `cut -c1-100` returns 100 characters under
`LANG=en_US.UTF-8` and an undecodable byte string with LANG unset.

Two fix directions, neither applied:
- swap this one site to the same python3 clipping approach; smallest and safest
- OR set `LANG` in the plist, which fixes the whole class at once but changes `sort`
  collation for every script in the tick — a broader behaviour change than this warrants on
  its own, and it should not be made casually just to tidy a log line
title: phase7-envelope truncates model output with cut -c, which counts bytes under launchd's C locale
